architecture.mechanism: Hydrophilic modification of the hollow-fiber membrane with polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) reduces protein adsorption to the membrane and stabilizes membrane permeability, so as fouling accumulates during a session the transmembrane pressure rise is blunted and filtrate flow and middle-molecule clearance are sustained.
architecture.intervention: Switch the in-center unit to a same-class, same-membrane-material high-flux hollow-fiber polysulfone dialyzer that carries PVP hydrophilic surface modification (e.g., FX CorAL-type dialyzer), leaving blood tubing, machine settings, session length (≤4 h 15 min), and blood-side sensing unchanged.
architecture.expected_effect: Slower, smaller TMP creep in the last 90 minutes of 4-hour sessions (fewer climbs from the set 50 mmHg toward the 100 mmHg alarm limit), reduced need for staff ultrafiltration-rate reductions, and better sustained β2-microglobulin clearance and filtrate flow late in treatment.
architecture.falsification_test: In vitro recirculation of a protein-containing plasma-substitute through the current and the PVP-modified polysulfone dialyzers at clinical blood/dialysate flows for 240 minutes, logging TMP every 10 minutes; falsified if the modified dialyzer's TMP increase is not substantially lower than control after 240 min (e.g., not ≤ ~50% of control) or if its post-fouling β2-microglobulin clearance is not the higher of the two.
